summary: This article explains how the Moon's gravity, with help from the Sun and Earth's spin, makes the sea rise and fall each day, why some tides are bigger than others, and how tides matter to people.
introduce: Read the title “Why the Sea Has Tides” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: lined up in a straight row
describes the small tides that come when the Sun and Moon pull at right angles
the difference between the lowest and the highest amount of something

challengeTerms.def: having to do with gravity, the force that pulls objects toward each other
one stage in a series of changes, such as the changing shapes of the Moon
meeting at a right angle, like the corner of a square

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that the Moon affects life on Earth every day? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain the difference between spring tides and neap tides.
struggling: Pre-teach aligned, neap, and range with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use gravitational, phase, and perpendicular in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
